sum: Nine days from Kathmandu: north along the ridge above Chautara by forest camps and herders' pastures to the five lakes of Panch Pokhari at about 4,100 m, then down to the road at Chhimti.

guide.note: The lakes and the upper ridge are inside Langtang National Park, and the Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023. Checks on the trail are inconsistent, and we know of no checkpost on this ridge. Here a guide is a practical need in any case: the trail is unmarked and faint across the pastures, mist is common, only people who have walked it know where the water is, and the camping crew has to be arranged through an agency.

access: Chautara is about 95 km from Kathmandu by the Araniko Highway and a side road from Dolalghat, four to six hours by bus or hired vehicle. A dirt road carries on along the ridge through Syaule to Sano Okhareni, and some groups ride that far. The trek ends at Chhimti, above Bhotang, where the bus to Kathmandu starts; the road down the Indrawati valley to Melamchi is rough and can close in the monsoon.

photo.a: A large dark-blue lake and several smaller ones lie in a brown, grassy bowl, with a rocky ridge on the right and a sea of white cloud beyond the rim.
photo.c: The lakes of Panch Pokhari, at about 4,100 m

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.

tips: Buy the Langtang National Park permit and the TIMS card in Kathmandu before you leave. We know of no counter on this side of the park.
Agree with your agency in writing what the crew will carry: tents, a kitchen, fuel and food for at least five days on the ridge.
Carry at least two litres of water each from every camp and treat all of it. Ask your guide each morning where the next source is.
Bring a four-season sleeping bag. Nights at Nasim Pati and the lakes are below freezing even in April and October.
Avoid the week of Janai Purnima in August unless you are going as a pilgrim. The shelters overflow and the trail is deep mud.

days.note: Out along the Araniko Highway to Dolalghat, then up a side road to the ridge-top bazaar of Chautara, the district headquarters of Sindhupalchok. Buy your last supplies here: beyond the town there is no bank and hardly a shop until the trek is over.

North along the ridge on a dirt road and the footpaths that cut its bends, through farm hamlets and the small bazaar of Syaule, with the Indrawati valley on your left and the Balephi on your right. It is a warm, dusty day with vehicles for company, which is why some groups ride it.

An hour's climb to the houses of Thulo Okhareni, then about four hours of steady ascent through oak and rhododendron forest to the clearing of Kami Kharka. You gain close to 850 m. Fill every bottle before you leave the village.

A shorter day along the forested crest, up and down over wooded knolls, to a pilgrims' rest place at about 3,000 m. Published times for this stage run from four to six hours and heights from 3,000 to 3,250 m, which shows how seldom it is measured.

The forest thins to rhododendron and grass as the ridge climbs. The trail keeps close to the crest, dropping into small saddles and climbing out again, to a camp in a notch at about 3,400 m. Nights are noticeably colder from here on.

A day of ridge walking over several tops, rocky in places, to the pilgrim shelters and seasonal teahouses of Nasim Pati. The trail from Bhotang comes up here, so you may meet other trekkers for the first time. If you have a headache tonight, stay a second night before going higher.

A steady climb of about 400 m over open, rocky ground to the bowl that holds the lakes. Arrive by lunch, walk round the shore to the Shiva shrine and keep the rim above the camp for sunrise. There is a pilgrims' shelter, and in season a hut may sell meals, but do not count on a bed.

Up before dawn for the view from the rim, then back to Nasim Pati and down the pilgrims' trail on the Bhotang side, steeply through forest, losing about 1,800 m in the day. It is very hard on the knees. Tupi Danda has simple lodges and the first phone signal for a week.

days.t: Tupi Danda to Chhimti, drive to Kathmandu
days.note: About two hours of steep descent to the road at Chhimti, then five to seven hours in a hired jeep down the Indrawati valley through Melamchi to Kathmandu, the first of them on rough road. If you are using the public bus, which leaves early, sleep at Chhimti and travel the next morning.
